title: Backcasting from 'Safety Disclosures Are Honest': Cross-Checking Lab Claims Against Independent Benchmarks

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Safety Disclosures Are Honest': Cross-Checking Lab Claims Against Independent Benchmarks

**Problem:** A success state where governance trusts lab self-reports requires those reports to match independent measurement. Labs report their own dangerous-capability eval results; without external cross-checks, optimistic or selectively-reported numbers could mislead regulators.

**Direction:** For 2-3 open or open-weight models whose developers published safety/capability claims, independently re-run a matching public benchmark on a single GPU and compare your measured numbers to the claimed ones. Document discrepancies, possible causes (elicitation, version, prompt differences), and a simple protocol for 'claim verification' that a third party could reuse.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'trustworthy self-reports' shows independent cross-checking as the precondition. Even one documented discrepancy demonstrates why third-party verification is necessary — directly serving the Open Problems verification agenda. Needs only open models and public benchmarks; the canonical outsider counterfactual against lab self-reporting.

**Relevant context:** FLI Index: implementation-over-commitments, naive elicitation under-reports; Open Problems in Technical AI Governance verification capacity; 'Frontier AI Auditing' (arXiv:2601.11699) on third-party assessment.
